newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan January export orders up 2.03 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan January export orders up 2.03 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Foreign orders for Taiwan goods rose 2.03 percent to US$9.872 billion in January compared to January 1996, the economics ministry said on Tuesday.
The official January export order figure was significantly higher than the average forecast of 1.58 percent that resulted from a February 14 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
That poll gave a wide range of forecasts, with the most bullish forecast at 4.9 percent increase over January 1996 and the most pessimistic forecasting a 2.1 percent year-on-year downturn.
National Securities was closest with its 2.0 percent forecast.
The following is a table of export data in million of U.S. dollars.
The ministry did not give a reason for the moderate growth.
Geographically, the United States remained Taiwan's biggest market with export orders rising 0.33 percent from a year ago to US$2.742 billion.
Hong Kong was next with orders totalling US$1.801 billion, but that figure was down 7.12 percent from January 1996. Orders from Europe grew 16.15 percent to US$1.697 billion.

In sectoral terms, telecommunication and informational products orders accounted for US$1.45 billion of the total, down 5.36 percent from a year ago. Electronics were second with US$1.37 billion, which was a 9.69 percent drop from January 1996.
Textile orders grew 12.98 percent to US$1.28 billion. Base metal products orders fell 6.93 percent to US$830 million.
Plastics were next with orders of US$610 million, followed by machinery orders with US$590 million.
